notes: Three scenarios, run repeatedly. Optimised for variance rather than coverage:
the citation flake was only visible because one section ran twice, so repeat
observations on a few scenarios say more than single observations on many.
Every scenario carries both answerable and unanswerable sections, so refusal
accuracy runs in both directions. An agent that refuses everything scores
perfectly on hallucination and is useless, and this set is built to catch that.
The corpus is 20 commission announcements. Sections 2 and 3 (broadcaster slate,
competing formats) have evidence. Sections 1, 4, 5 and 6 ask for territory
viewing data, audience appetite, format fit reasoning and risk assessment, and
none of that exists in the corpus. The labels below record that, they do not
aspire to something the corpus could support.
The 'plan' field is populated once by 'python eval.py --plans' and committed, so
repeat runs do not pay for the planner and every run is measured against the
same plan. Plan-stage variance is excluded from this harness by construction.
That is a real limitation and it is stated in the results rather than hidden:
a planner eval is a separate instrument that does not exist yet.
